translation_notes: the four URIRef("...") term constructors become IRI islands <...>; the transpiler emits exactly URIRef('...'), so the change is purely notational
with the term constructor absorbed by the notation, URIRef is no longer needed: 'from rdflib import Graph, URIRef' becomes 'from rdflib import Graph' (same style as the reference example)

negative finding: only 4 of the 8 RDF operations are expressible - the four Graph(store=..., identifier=..., bind_namespaces='core').parse(file=f) calls are graph *plumbing* (named graphs over an explicit Memory store, pickled afterwards) that no island form covers; g{ ... } builds a fresh default Graph and cannot be given a store or an identifier

context shim: pyshacl/ in the example directory is a stub package whose pyshacl/monkey/__init__.py is a verbatim copy of RDFLib/pySHACL@469cca7a22 (its only dependencies are rdflib and packaging); this keeps 'from pyshacl.monkey import apply_patches' unchanged on both sides - no import line was edited

driver.py copies the four .ttl assets (~1.4 MB, too large to vendor) from the corpus checkout into a scratch directory and runs both representations there, since the region reads ./*.ttl and writes ./*.pickle relative to the current directory; the scratch directory is removed afterwards and the corpus copy is never written to

driver limitation: module-state comparison observes the graph g (the last of the four, 420 triples) and stdout; the `identifier` URIRefs themselves are not compared by the harness because they are not Graphs, so the four islands are additionally checked by inspecting the transpiler output
